opening.text: A builder uses a plumb line to check that a wall is straight. It is a string with a weight. Gravity pulls it true. If the wall leans, the plumb line shows it. Honesty is like that. It is the line we measure ourselves against. When our words and actions hang straight, we can build on them.

mainMessage.text: Honesty is a straight line in a leaning world. It builds trust, peace and strength.

blocks.text: **More than not lying** Honesty is bigger than avoiding lies. The Lord asked His people to deal fairly with each other.
And let every man deal honestly, and be alike among this people, and receive alike, that ye may be one, even as I have commanded you.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is more than not lying.
It is more than not lying.
**Truth in every form** Honesty shows up in what we say, how we live and what we love.
We believe in being honest, true, chaste, benevolent, virtuous, and in doing good to all men;
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
It is truth telling, truth speaking, truth living, and truth loving.
Truth is a way of life.
**It guides us** A straight line shows us where we are. Integrity does the same. It points us the right way.
The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is a moral compass to guide us in our lives.
It guides us.
**What dishonesty costs** A crooked wall gets worse with every row of bricks. Small lies add up. In the end, the person who lied pays the most.
But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
By being dishonest, people only cheat themselves.
The cost is ours.
**True to God and to others** Integrity means being the same person everywhere, in public and in private. Job held to it even under pressure.
God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Living a life of integrity requires us to be true to God, to each other, and to our divine identity.
Be the same person everywhere.
**Words and actions line up** A wall is straight when every part lines up. Our words and our actions should line up too.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Saying we have integrity is insufficient if our actions are inconsistent with our words.
Let actions match words.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they chose to be honest, even when it cost them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nathanael, a man without guile

blocks.text: When Jesus Christ first saw Nathanael, He said something about his character.
Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!
The Savior saw Nathanael's heart and loved what He saw. Nathanael was the same on the outside as on the inside. That is the straight line.

application.text: First, think of one place where your words and actions don't line up. Second, fix that one thing this week. Third, ask God to help you stay true.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God is a God of truth. I know honesty brings peace of mind. I know Jesus Christ is the way, the truth and the life. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A clean window lets the light in. You can see through it. A dirty window does the opposite. It hides what is on the other side. Honesty makes us clear windows. People can see us as we are. And that is why they trust us.

mainMessage.text: Honesty makes us clear windows. We are open, trusted and at peace.

blocks.text: **Seeing straight through** Being honest means no hidden corners. God asked His people to deal openly with each other.
And let every man deal honestly, and be alike among this people, and receive alike, that ye may be one, even as I have commanded you.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is more than not lying.
There is more to see.
**Clear all the way across** The window is clear in every part. Honesty reaches our words, our choices and our love.
We believe in being honest, true, chaste, benevolent, virtuous, and in doing good to all men;
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
It is truth telling, truth speaking, truth living, and truth loving.
Clear all the way.
**Light for the road** A clear window lets in light. Integrity lights our path.
The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is a moral compass to guide us in our lives.
Light shows the way.
**Dust builds up** A window gets dirty a little at a time. So does a life. Small untruths cloud the glass until we can't see out.
But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
By being dishonest, people only cheat themselves.
It clouds our own view.
**The same inside and out** A window shows what is really there. We can be the same in public and in private.
God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Living a life of integrity requires us to be true to God, to each other, and to our divine identity.
Inside and out.
**Showing what we say** People don't only hear us. They watch us. What they see should match what they hear.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Saying we have integrity is insufficient if our actions are inconsistent with our words.
Words and actions agree.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they put something right. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Zacchaeus makes it right

blocks.text: Zacchaeus was a tax collector. He had taken more than he should. After meeting Jesus Christ, he made a promise.
And Zacchæus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
He didn't make excuses. He named the wrong and fixed it, and he gave more than was asked. Honesty can start again at any time.

application.text: First, think of one thing you can set right. Second, do it this week, even if it is small. Third, notice how you feel afterward.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know honesty brings a clear conscience. I know God trusts those who are true. I know Jesus Christ is the light of the world. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A compass has one job. It points north. It doesn't change its mind because the storm is loud or the crowd goes another way. A hiker who trusts it gets home. Honesty works like that. It points the same way every time, so we can find our way when everything else is confusing.

mainMessage.text: Honesty is a compass for life. It keeps us on course when the path is hard to see.

blocks.text: **More than not lying** The needle does more than avoid south. It points one way. Honesty is bigger than avoiding lies.
And let every man deal honestly, and be alike among this people, and receive alike, that ye may be one, even as I have commanded you.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is more than not lying.
It points one way.
**Four directions of truth** A compass has four directions. Honesty has four, too.
We believe in being honest, true, chaste, benevolent, virtuous, and in doing good to all men;
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
It is truth telling, truth speaking, truth living, and truth loving.
Four directions, one truth.
**Trust the needle** When the trail disappears, we trust the compass. Integrity will guide us when other things fail.
The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is a moral compass to guide us in our lives.
Trust the needle.
**Bending the needle** Hold a magnet near a compass, and it points the wrong way. A small lie does that. We think we are on course, but we are drifting.
But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
By being dishonest, people only cheat themselves.
We only fool ourselves.
**One direction in every place** A compass doesn't change in the city or in the forest. Our integrity shouldn't either.
God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Living a life of integrity requires us to be true to God, to each other, and to our divine identity.
Same way, every place.
**Walking the direction** Knowing north isn't enough. We have to walk it. The same goes for honesty.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Saying we have integrity is insufficient if our actions are inconsistent with our words.
Walk it.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they were open to being checked, and nothing was hidden. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Samuel's farewell

blocks.text: Samuel was old and was stepping down as Israel's leader. He asked the people to speak up if he had ever wronged them.

Behold, here I am: witness against me before the Lord, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.
Samuel had nothing to hide. His whole life had pointed the same way. That is what honesty gives us: freedom to be seen.

application.text: First, ask yourself where you feel pulled off course. Second, pick one honest habit, like telling the whole truth even when it is small. Third, practice it for a week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know honesty is a guide God gave us. I know it keeps us safe. I know Jesus Christ never changed course and never will. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Trust is like a bank account. Every honest act is a deposit. Every dishonest act is a withdrawal. When the account is full, people trust you with big things. When it is empty, even true words are doubted. And it takes a long time to rebuild.

mainMessage.text: Honesty builds an account of trust. Every honest choice adds to it.

blocks.text: **Deposits, not just avoiding debt** An account isn't only about avoiding overdraft. It is about building something. Honesty is more than avoiding lies.
And let every man deal honestly, and be alike among this people, and receive alike, that ye may be one, even as I have commanded you.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is more than not lying.
Build, don't just avoid.
**Every kind of deposit** We can deposit in many ways: what we say, how we live and what we love.
We believe in being honest, true, chaste, benevolent, virtuous, and in doing good to all men;
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
It is truth telling, truth speaking, truth living, and truth loving.
Deposit in every way.
**What the account guides** A full account lets us make good choices. Integrity guides us to decisions we can stand behind.
The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is a moral compass to guide us in our lives.
It guides our choices.
**The withdrawal** A dishonest act takes out more than it seems. The lie may save a moment. But the cost lands on us.
But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
By being dishonest, people only cheat themselves.
The cost lands on us.
**Trusted by God and people** The best account is held with God and with the people around us. Integrity builds both.
God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Living a life of integrity requires us to be true to God, to each other, and to our divine identity.
Trusted by God and others.
**Paying what we promise** Promises are checks. They have to be honored. Words that aren't kept leave us overdrawn.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Saying we have integrity is insufficient if our actions are inconsistent with our words.
Keep your word.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone trusted them because they were honest. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Hyrum Smith

blocks.text: The Lord spoke about Hyrum Smith, who was Joseph Smith's brother.

And again, verily I say unto you, blessed is my servant Hyrum Smith; for I, the Lord, love him because of the integrity of his heart, and because he loveth that which is right before me, saith the Lord.
The Lord didn't name Hyrum's talents. He named the integrity of his heart. That is a full account of trust, built one honest act at a time.

application.text: First, think of a promise you made recently. Second, keep it this week. Third, make one new honest deposit each day.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that honesty builds trust with God and with people. I know the Lord loves those whose hearts are true. I know Jesus Christ is faithful to every promise. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A bridge only works if every beam is sound. One hidden crack, and the whole thing is at risk. People cross bridges without checking each beam. They trust the builder. Honesty is what makes us a bridge people can cross. Others can lean on our word without fear.

mainMessage.text: Honesty makes us a bridge people can trust. It holds weight when others lean on it.

blocks.text: **More than a clean surface** A bridge isn't strong just because it looks good. Honesty goes deeper than not lying.
And let every man deal honestly, and be alike among this people, and receive alike, that ye may be one, even as I have commanded you.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is more than not lying.
It goes deeper.
**Strong in every beam** Every part of the bridge matters. Honesty reaches our speech, our living and our loving.
We believe in being honest, true, chaste, benevolent, virtuous, and in doing good to all men;
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
It is truth telling, truth speaking, truth living, and truth loving.
Every beam counts.
**It carries us across** A bridge takes us where we want to go. Integrity carries us through hard places.
The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
Honesty is a moral compass to guide us in our lives.
It carries us across.
**The hidden crack** A hidden crack grows. A dishonest choice does the same. It weakens us before we notice.
But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.
President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Honesty, a Moral Compass” from the October 1996 general conference.
By being dishonest, people only cheat themselves.
The crack is ours.
**Anchored in God** A bridge is anchored on both banks. Our integrity is anchored in God and in the people we serve.
God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Living a life of integrity requires us to be true to God, to each other, and to our divine identity.
Anchored on both sides.
**Built, not just drawn** A plan on paper crosses nothing. The bridge has to be built. Our words have to be carried out.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
Elder Jack N. Gerard of the Seventy said this in his talk “Integrity: A Christlike Attribute” from the April 2024 general conference.
Saying we have integrity is insufficient if our actions are inconsistent with our words.
Build what you say.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they were tempted to hide something and chose to tell the truth. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Ananias and the half-truth

blocks.text: Ananias sold land and gave part of the money to the Church. He said it was all of it.

But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land? Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.
He didn't have to give anything. The wrong was in pretending. We can't fool God, and we don't need to. Being plain and true is enough.

application.text: First, check one area of your life for a hidden crack, like a half-truth or an exaggeration. Second, fix it. Third, pray for help to be a bridge others can cross.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God sees our hearts and loves us. I know honesty gives peace that nothing else can. I know Jesus Christ is the bridge between us and our Father. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
